summary: The editor's decisions on the four 3.3 sentences that broke an earlier ruling, which the author left to best judgement (2026-10-25, review/questions_3_3.md). In the lexicon, one: 3.2:G147's example "Peta da Amerika" reads "li lira de Amerika", as the ruling's text gives it; the old example is archived.

ops.reason: The author left this to the editor (2026-10-25). 3.2:G147 says "de + the name means from the place", and a noun phrase takes de, not a prepositional phrase, after it (2.5:G98): "a song from America" is li lira de Amerika. Peta da Amerika had neither a verb nor a place for its da phrase. For a person, Peta ka da Amerika (Peta is from America) also reads clean.
